label: conj:cyclotomic-boundary-at-keystone
title: The Habiro-tail cyclotomic boundary sits at the quintic order: $D(n)$ is cyclotomic $\iff n \leq 5$
html:
Conjecture. The Habiro-tail cyclotomic boundary sits at the quintic order: D(n) is cyclotomic \iff n \leq 5

Conjecture (cyclotomic boundary at the quintic order).

The binding q-deformation of the na-Stokes period S(n) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim_q(\lambda) satisfies the recurrence

S(n) \;=\; S(n-1) \;+\; [n-1]_q\,S(n-2) \;+\; D(n),

whose deviation term D(n) — the Habiro tail — carries a universal (q-1)^2 double root at q=1 and is bar-even (D(1/q)=D(q)). The conjecture asserts that D(n) is cyclotomic — a product of cyclotomic polynomials (times the (q-1)^2 factor and a q-monomial) — if and only if n \leq 5, where 5 is the quintic order S_5 \supset A_5.

The alignment. The cyclotomic-pure regime n \leq 5 coincides exactly with the framework's calibration orders and the quintic order:

\{\,n \leq 5 : D(n)\text{ cyclotomic}\,\}
\;=\;
\underbrace{\{n=2,3,4\}}_{\text{calibration orders } c=1,2,3}
\;\cup\;
\underbrace{\{n=5\}}_{S_5\text{ quintic order}}.

The first non-cyclotomic (non-q-holonomic) content appears at the first body order n=6 that is neither a calibration nor the quintic order.

The arithmetic mechanism. At q=1 one has S(n)|_{q=1} = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} f^\lambda = I(n), the involution / telephone numbers (OEIS A000085; the Frobenius–Schur identity, proved for all n by RSK: involutions \leftrightarrow SYT). So S(n) is the q-deformed involution number — a Rogers–Szegő / q-Hermite moment — and the recurrence above is the q-lift of I(n)=I(n-1)+(n-1)I(n-2), with D(n) its deviation. Prior analysis of this q-involution kernel establishes the tail's structure: a (q-1)^2 double root times a bar-even cofactor that is cyclotomic through n=5 and acquires a genuine non-cyclotomic, non-q-holonomic factor from n=6 — the same non-holonomicity that obstructs any fixed-order closed form for S(n). This is the mechanism that governs D(n): it is a property of cancellation in the alternating sum, not of any individual quantum dimension.

Why the individual quantum dimensions do not locate the boundary. Every \dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q!/\prod_c [h(c)]_q is a product of cyclotomic polynomials for every n (a ratio of cyclotomic products that is a polynomial). So cyclotomic-purity of the individual dimensions does not distinguish n=5 from n=6: at both orders all \dim_q(\lambda) are cyclotomic. In particular the McKay observation below — that at n=5 the four classes carry single quantum integers while at n=6 most are compound products of several [m]_q — is a single-[m]_q-vs-product distinction, not a cyclotomic-vs-non-cyclotomic one (a product of several cyclotomics is still cyclotomic). It does not, by itself, supply the arithmetic mechanism above.

The McKay coincidence (rep-theory, link unproven). At the quintic order n=5 the four conjugation classes \{\lambda,\lambda'\} of S_5 carry quantum dimensions equal to the E_8 Coxeter marks [\mathrm{mark}]_q:

\dim_q(5)=[1]_q,\quad
\dim_q(4,1)=[4]_q,\quad
\dim_q(3,2)=[5]_q,\quad
\dim_q(3,1,1)=[5]_q+1,

because A_5 \cong 2I/\{\pm 1\} is the icosahedral group and 2I \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_8 (McKay). The McKay–ADE ladder of alternating groups is finite: A_4 \cong tetrahedral (2T \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_6), A_5 \cong icosahedral (2I \leftrightarrow \widehat{E}_8), and A_6 \cong \mathrm{PSL}(2,9) is not a binary polyhedral group. Thus A_5 is the last alternating group that is the rotation group of a Platonic solid, and A_6 (n=6) is the first non-McKay. That the McKay-mark structure exits at the same order the tail leaves the cyclotomic ring is a coincidence of orders; by the caveat above it does not act through cyclotomic-purity of the dimensions, and its bearing on the arithmetic mechanism is unproven.

Status — three tiers of correlation, not to be conflated.

  1. Arithmetic (the substance): D(n) is non-cyclotomic from n=6. This is verified through n=11 but not proved for all n \geq 6; the cofactor's non-q-holonomic degree growth is the structural reason, not yet a proof. Generic high-degree bar-even integer polynomials are non-cyclotomic, so non-cyclotomicity is the expected outcome — the content is entirely that n \leq 5 are cyclotomic, and that "for all n \geq 6, with no exceptions" is what a proof must supply.
  2. Alignment: that boundary coincides with {calibration \cup quintic} orders \{2,3,4\}\cup\{5\}.
  3. Rep-theory: the McKay-mark / S_6-outer-automorphism coincidence at n=6.

The causation — whether the A_5 \to A_6 McKay exit or the S_6 outer automorphism forces the boundary — is unproved, and the route through the single-vs-compound quantum dimensions does not establish it. What can be said is the dovetail with S(n)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\dim_q(\lambda)= \sum_\lambda W_\lambda: the same S_5 whose quantum dimensions are the E_8 marks carries the Verlinde measure W_\lambda. Specific root magnitudes are not interpreted.

Partial formalization. The Lean module QOU.Mass.CyclotomicBoundaryKeystone formalizes what is honestly provable. Sorry-free: the Tier-1 base-case factorizations D(4)=\Phi_1^2\Phi_3 and D(5)=2\,\Phi_1^2\Phi_2^2\Phi_3\Phi_6 (with the factors verified equal to Mathlib's cyclotomic polynomials); the palindrome identity C_6(z)=z^4\,\tilde C(z+z^{-1}); and the full n = 6 non-cyclotomicity of the deg-8 core C_6 — that C_6 is not a product of cyclotomic polynomials — derived using only the elementary direction of Kronecker's dichotomy (roots of cyclotomics are roots of unity, hence of modulus 1), not the hard converse. The entire n = 6 chain rests on a single cited classical input: that \tilde C(y)=y^4+4y^3+2y^2-10y-8 has a non-real root (immediate from \mathrm{disc}(\tilde C)=-44208<0; Mathlib lacks the discriminant–root-product bridge). The full Tier-2 claim (non-cyclotomic for all n\geq 6) is not formalized — it remains verified-through-n=11.
